texts.preamble: Rehmatali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 August, 2019
texts.facts: Applicant/accused has preferred this revision petition under Section 397 read with Section 401 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short "The Code") against the order dated 27/04/2019 passed by Special Judge (NDPS ACT), District Mandsaur, in Special Sessions Trial No.35/2019, whereby the trial Court has rejected the application filed on behalf of the applicant/accused praying for re-testing of second sample of the seized contraband article from the Central Revenues and Control Laboratory (CRCL), New Delhi. 02. Brief facts of the case are that on 13/10/2018, at about 3.40 pm, 4.00 kgs of smack has been seized from the possession of the applicant which was being transported in his Maruti Alto car bearing Registration No.MP 14 CC 2397. Sample of the contraband article has been taken and sent for examination to Regional Forensic Laboratory, Rao, District Indore. Wherein, on examination, it has been found to be Di-acetyl Morphine (smack). After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed on 09/04/2019 before the Special Court (NDPS), Mandsaur. On 15/04/2019, the applicant/accused had moved an application for sending the second sample of seized contraband for analysis to CRCL, New Delhi. 03. Learned trial Judge, rejected the application on the context of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 'Thana Singh vs. Central Bureau of Narcotics, reported as (2013)2 SCC 590 holding that under extremely exceptional circumstances the re-testing of second sample of the seized contraband article can be ordered and there is no such circumstance available in the present case.
texts.arguments: In the case of Thana Singh Vs. CBN (Supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court issued the guidelines for re- testing /re-sampling of the contraband articles seized under the 'NDPS Act'. Relevant paragraphs of the judgment is reproduced hereunder:- NDPS courts seem to be permitting re-testing nonetheless by taking resort to either some High Court judgments [See: State of Kerala Vs. Deepak. P. Shah[5]; Nihal Khan Vs. The State (Govt. of NCT Delhi)[6]] or perhaps to Sections 79 and 80 of the NDPS Act which permit application of the Customs Act, 1962 and the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. In the present case, learned counsel for the applicant has put forth his submissions that no contraband article has been recovered from the possession of the applicant. 07. Learned Panel Lawyer opposes the prayer by contending that no ground is available for sending the second sample to CRCL, New Delhi for re-testing hence he prays for rejection of the application.
